notes:
Status: effectively closed-lost. Verdant chose competitor (BlueModel) after POC failure and procurement freeze. CRM notes from AE/SE/POC: 
- 2025-11: inbound from partner lead; initial intro call (Ethan).
- 2025-12: discovery with ML infra + security (Diego on call). Strong interest: reduce inference cost for chat + robust structured invoice extraction.
- 2026-01-12: demo (seeded dataset). Showed tool-calling flows for payment orchestration. Good reception on latency & cost dashboard, but ops flagged structured-output reliability concerns.
- 2026-01-20: POC started (small canary, Dedicated pool). POC goal: 95% valid JSON outputs for invoice extraction + sub-150ms median token latency for interactive agent.
- 2026-02-02: POC failure mode observed — after a model/quantization change we recommended, system returned malformed JSON and incorrect invoice line-items on 18% of test prompts. Broke downstream parsers -> pipeline exceptions. SE reproduced locally. Ticket JIRA-3721 logged.
- 2026-02-07: Security review escalated. Verdant infosec requires ISO27001 evidence and strict audit_logging with 1y retention; they also want EU data residency for EU customers. Our private offering not yet fully validated for their residency requirement.
- 2026-02-12: BlueModel submitted counter-offer: committed structured-output SLAs in writing, plus white-glove onboarding. Verdant procurement asked for a signed reliability commitment.
- 2026-02-15: Final procurement call. Head of ML: "We can't risk production regressions — customers are furious when invoices are parsed wrong." CTO recently departed; no clear internal champion remains. Procurement freezes headcount spend.
- 2026-02-18: AE update: Verdant marks internal vendor selection toward BlueModel. Decision: pause Redwood engagement.
- Follow-up attempts: 2 emails, 1 voicemail, no substantive reply since 2026-02-18.

Key technical takeaways (from SE notes):
- Root cause for regression: model variant + quantization profile change produced edge-case tokenization differences that broke the tool-calling/JSON schema enforcement path.
- Incumbent/BlueModel uses a constraint-enforced structured-output wrapper in their serving layer; Verdant prioritized determinism over raw token-cost savings.
- Our Optimize recommendations lowered cost but increased variability for strict-schema outputs; tradeoff not acceptable for billing pipelines.

Sales/ops actions taken:
- Escalated to PM and inference team (Diego). Proposed a tight canary with schema-enforcement fallback and additional tests. PM noted required infra changes would delay timeline by ~8 weeks.
- Legal reviewed but Verdant procurement required SLA-level reliability guarantees we couldn't sign at POC stage.

Quotes: 
- Head of ML (Verdant): "If even 1 in 50 invoices is wrong, we take a customer hit. We need guarantees."
- VP Ops (Verdant): "Your latency/cost story is great, but the risk isn't worth the savings right now."

Next steps recommended internally:
- Close as lost, create post-mortem with inference team and product to capture technical fixes (schema enforcement, stricter evals for structured-output).
- Add Verdant use-case to Optimize prioritization for deterministic structured-output flows.
- Re-open cadence in 6 months; attempt to re-engage once infra changes shipped.
